title: OPNsense Exporter (Grafana 11/12 compatibility)
description: Comprehensive single-pane OPNsense firewall dashboard. Tabs and rows auto-hide when their metrics are absent. Built from grafana/build_dashboard.py. — COMPATIBILITY BUILD, generated from the canonical Grafana 13 schema-v2 dashboard for Grafana 11.5.0 and 12.4.0. Carries only the panels that are unconditional on every OPNsense box: classic schema has no conditional rendering, so a plugin-gated tab would show permanently empty panels here. Use grafana/dashboard.json on Grafana 13+.

list.name: device
list.label: Device (pf/netflow/interfaces)
list.definition: query_result(group by (opnsense_instance, device) (label_join(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_packets_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}, "device", "", "interface") or label_join(opnsense_netflow_cache_packets_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}, "device", "", "interface") or label_join(opnsense_vnstat_bytes_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}, "device", "", "interface") or opnsense_interfaces_info{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance",device!=""} or opnsense_flow_interface_info{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance",device!=""}))

query.query: query_result(group by (opnsense_instance, device) (label_join(opnsense_firewall_in_ipv4_pass_packets_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}, "device", "", "interface") or label_join(opnsense_netflow_cache_packets_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}, "device", "", "interface") or label_join(opnsense_vnstat_bytes_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}, "device", "", "interface") or opnsense_interfaces_info{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance",device!=""} or opnsense_flow_interface_info{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance",device!=""}))

list.name: has_go_runtime
list.label: has_go_runtime
list.definition: query_result(go_goroutines{job=~"opnsense.*"} * on(job, instance) group_left() max by (job, instance) (opnsense_up{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}))

query.query: query_result(go_goroutines{job=~"opnsense.*"} * on(job, instance) group_left() max by (job, instance) (opnsense_up{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}))

list.name: has_otlp
list.label: has_otlp
list.definition: query_result(opnsense_exporter_otlp_enabled * on(job, instance) group_left() max by (job, instance) (opnsense_up{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}))

query.query: query_result(opnsense_exporter_otlp_enabled * on(job, instance) group_left() max by (job, instance) (opnsense_up{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}))

panels.title: Firmware Info
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_info: firmware metadata labels.

panels.title: Needs Reboot
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_needs_reboot: 1 if a reboot is required.

panels.title: Upgrade Needs Reboot
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_upgrade_needs_reboot: 1 if pending upgrade requires reboot.

panels.title: Last Firmware Check
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_last_check_timestamp_seconds: Unix timestamp of last update check.

panels.title: Update Check
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_update_check_success: 1 when the firewall's stored update check reached, authenticated and verified its repository. 0 means the check RAN AND FAILED (DNS, subscription, fingerprint, unavailable release train) — which without this metric is indistinguishable from a healthy check with no pending updates. No data means no check has been stored yet. Reflects the stored result of the box's own check as seen through the exporter's firmware response cache, so a change can take up to --exporter.firmware-cache-ttl (default 12h) to show up.

panels.title: Pending Download
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_pending_download_bytes: total download size of the pending update, parsed from the stored check's mixed-unit download_size list (base-2). No data means either no stored check or a value that could not be parsed unambiguously — never a fabricated 0.

panels.title: New Packages
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_new_packages_count: count of newly available packages.

panels.title: Upgrade Packages
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_upgrade_packages_count: count of packages with available upgrades.

panels.title: Downgrade Packages
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_downgrade_packages_count: count of packages available to downgrade.

panels.title: Reinstall Packages
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_reinstall_packages_count: count of packages available to reinstall.

panels.title: Remove Packages
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_remove_packages_count: count of packages the pending update would remove.

panels.title: Upgrade Sets
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_upgrade_sets_count: count of pending upgrade sets (the synthetic base/kernel entries of a major or point upgrade, not ordinary packages).

panels.title: Update Check Components
panels.description: opnsense_firmware_update_check_state: current state of each update-check component. connection: error/unauthenticated/misconfigured/unresolved/ok. repository: error/untrusted/unsigned/revoked/incomplete/forbidden/ok. Anything else, including a future upstream state, collapses to unknown.

panels.title: Last Config Backup
panels.description: opnsense_backup_last_timestamp_seconds: Unix timestamp of the newest retained config backup. Compare against time() to catch silent backup failure.

panels.title: Retained Backups
panels.description: opnsense_backup_count: number of config backups OPNsense currently retains.

panels.title: Last Backup Size
panels.description: opnsense_backup_last_size_bytes: size of the newest retained config backup.

panels.title: ZFS Boot Environments Supported

panels.title: Active Boot Environment Created
panels.description: opnsense_snapshots_active_created_timestamp_seconds: creation time of the currently active boot environment. Absent when none is marked active (e.g. unsupported filesystem) — are pre-upgrade snapshots actually being made?

panels.description: opnsense_auth_users_expired: local users whose account expiry date has passed. Should normally be 0 — a non-zero value is a stale account still able to authenticate up to the point OPNsense itself enforces the expiry.

panels.title: Auth Groups

panels.title: Interface RX Throughput
panels.description: Bytes received per second × 8 = bits per second.

panels.title: Interface TX Throughput
panels.description: Bytes transmitted per second × 8 = bits per second. Shown as negative-Y by convention.

panels.title: Packets RX
panels.description: Packets received per second.

panels.title: Packets TX
panels.description: Packets transmitted per second.

panels.title: Multicast Traffic
panels.description: Multicast packets per second.

panels.title: Interface Errors
panels.description: Input and output errors per second.

panels.title: Collisions
panels.description: Collision events per second.

panels.title: Send Queue Length
panels.description: Current and maximum send queue length (instantaneous gauges).

panels.title: Queue Drops
panels.description: Send-queue and input-queue drops per second.

panels.title: Link State
panels.description: 1 = Up (green), 0 = Down (red), 2 = Unknown (yellow). Unknown is reported by the kernel for carrier-less pseudo-devices (PPPoE, tun/tailscale) and is not a fault - alert on Down (0), not not-Up.

panels.title: Interface Info (MTU / Line Rate / Device / Type)
panels.description: Static per-interface properties: MTU, negotiated line rate, OS device name, and type.

panels.title: Admin Status
panels.description: opnsense_interfaces_admin_up: 1 = administratively up (ifconfig UP flag), 0 = admin down. Admin up + Link State down = no carrier.

panels.title: Interface Identity (media / VLAN / link type)
panels.description: opnsense_interfaces_info: interface identity from the overview API (media/duplex, link type, VLAN topology).

panels.title: Unknown Protocol Packets
panels.description: opnsense_interfaces_unknown_protocol_packets_total: rate of packets delivered to this interface that the network stack could not classify (kernel "packets for unknown protocol" counter). Sustained non-zero traffic here is worth investigating - it never reaches a normal protocol handler.

panels.title: Interface Attach / Stats Reset Age

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (opnsense_system_uptime_seconds{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"} - on(opnsense_instance) group_right() opnsense_interfaces_attach_or_statistics_reset_uptime_seconds{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance",interface=~"$interface"})

panels.description: opnsense_system_uptime_seconds - opnsense_interfaces_attach_or_statistics_reset_uptime_seconds: how long ago this interface was attached OR had its statistics explicitly reset - the kernel marker cannot distinguish the two. Only emitted when the box reports the marker. A sudden drop toward 0 across every counter on one interface, paired with this age resetting too, means the interface was recreated or its stats were reset - not a real traffic drop or an exporter bug.

panels.title: Network / Gateways & WAN — Status & Alarm Events
Gateway Status
panels.description: 0=Offline, 1=Online, 2=Unknown, 3=Pending, 4=Packetloss, 5=Latency, 6=Offline (forced). Label default_gateway is included in series.

panels.title: Gateway Alarm Events

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sum by (opnsense_instance, gateway, event) (rate(opnsense_log_events_gateway_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance",event=~"alarm_started|alarm_cleared"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: Rate of dpinger gateway alarm transitions. alarm_started marks none -> down; alarm_cleared marks down -> none. This complements the current Gateway Status timeline; it is absent until syslog shipping sees a matching dpinger line.

panels.title: Gateway RTT
panels.description: Average RTT and RTT standard deviation (RTTd) in milliseconds.

panels.title: RTT Thresholds
panels.description: Configured low/high RTT alarm thresholds per gateway.

panels.title: Packet Loss %
panels.description: Current packet loss percentage per gateway.

panels.title: Loss Thresholds
panels.description: Configured low/high packet-loss alarm thresholds per gateway.

panels.title: Gateway Info
panels.description: Static gateway configuration (info metric — value is always 1).

panels.title: Gateway Monitor Info
panels.description: Gateway monitoring configuration (info metric — value is always 1).

panels.title: Gateway Flags (force_down / virtual / dynamic / priority)
panels.description: Per-gateway boolean flags and routing priority (lower value = higher priority).

panels.title: Probe Configuration
panels.description: ICMP probe timing configuration per gateway.

panels.title: ARP Entries
panels.description: Total number of ARP table entries currently known (low-cardinality aggregate, always emitted).

panels.title: ARP Entries by Interface

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (count by (opnsense_instance, interface_description)(opnsense_arp_table_entries{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}))

panels.description: ARP entry count grouped by interface. Requires --exporter.enable-arp-details (#125).

panels.title: ARP Table Detail
panels.description: Full ARP table — all entries with their IP, MAC, hostname, interface, and flags.

panels.title: NDP Entries
panels.description: Total number of NDP (IPv6 neighbor) entries currently known (low-cardinality aggregate, always emitted).

panels.title: NDP Entries by Interface

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (count by (opnsense_instance, interface_description)(opnsense_ndp_entries{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}))

panels.description: NDP entry count grouped by interface. Requires --exporter.enable-ndp-details (#125).

panels.title: NDP Table Detail
panels.description: Full NDP (IPv6 neighbor discovery) table — all entries with IP, MAC, interface, and type.

panels.title: Discovered Hosts by Interface
panels.description: Number of hosts in the discovered-host inventory per interface. source=discovery means the hostwatch daemon is enabled (persistent inventory, survives reboots and cache expiry); source=arp-ndp means it is disabled and this is a live ARP/NDP-table fallback (see the ARP/NDP rows above) with no history.

panels.title: Recently Seen Hosts (15m) by Interface
panels.description: Subset of the discovered-host inventory last seen within 15 minutes, per interface. Always 0 for source=arp-ndp, which carries no last_seen timestamp to judge recency from. A sustained drop signals hosts going quiet on that interface.

panels.title: TCP Packets (rate)
panels.description: Rate of TCP packets sent and received.

panels.title: TCP Connection Lifecycle (rate)
panels.description: Rate of TCP connection lifecycle events.

panels.title: TCP Retransmit, Keepalive & Queue (rate)
panels.description: Rate of TCP retransmits, keepalive events, syncache activity, and listen queue overflows.

panels.title: TCP Connection Drops by Reason (rate)
panels.description: opnsense_protocol_tcp_connection_drops_by_reason_total: cumulative TCP connections dropped by reason (retransmit_timeout, persist_timeout, finwait2_timeout, keepalive) — kernel-lifetime counters that reset on reboot. A reason series only appears when the box reports that wire field, so an older box simply omits reasons it does not send rather than reporting zero. Distinguishes WAN loss, stalled applications, state-lifetime cleanup, and keepalive failure without a packet capture.

panels.title: TCP Throughput (rate)
panels.description: TCP byte throughput (bytes per second). Includes duplicate and retransmitted bytes.

panels.title: TCP Segments Updated RTT (rate)
panels.description: Rate of TCP segments that caused an RTT sample update.

panels.title: TCP Connections by State (now)
panels.description: Current distribution of TCP connections across states (gauge).

panels.title: TCP ECN Packets (rate)
panels.description: opnsense_protocol_tcp_ecn_packets_total: TCP packets carrying an ECN mark, by direction (received/sent) and mark (ce/ect0/ect1). The received direction is resolved across the 26.1.11 key rename; sent is 26.1.11+ only.

panels.title: TCP AccECN Handshakes (rate, 26.1.11+)
panels.description: opnsense_protocol_tcp_ecn_accecn_handshakes_total: FreeBSD 15 AccECN handshake SYNs by mark (ce/ect0/ect1/nonect). OPNsense 26.1.11+ only.

panels.title: TCP SYN Cookies (rate, 26.7+)
panels.description: opnsense_protocol_tcp_syncookies_total: SYN cookies by result (sent/received/failed/spurious). Replaces the legacy syncache sent-cookies/receivd-cookies pair, which never fed a metric. OPNsense 26.7+ only.

panels.title: TCP Acks For Data (rate, 26.7+)
panels.description: opnsense_protocol_tcp_received_acks_for_data_total: ACKs received for data by reason (not_yet_sent/never_been_sent/being_too_old) — the 26.7 three-way split of the legacy received-acks-for-unsent-data aggregate, which never fed a metric. OPNsense 26.7+ only.

panels.title: TCP Connections by State (over time)
panels.description: Number of TCP connections by state (gauge — current value, not rate).

panels.title: UDP Packets (rate)
panels.description: Rate of UDP datagrams received, delivered, and output.

panels.title: BPF Packet Counters (rate)
panels.description: BPF packet counters (cumulative) per (process, interface) aggregation. Aggregation sums entries with the same process+interface labels.

panels.title: BPF Buffer Sizes
panels.description: BPF store and hold buffer sizes in bytes per (process, interface). These are gauges — the kernel may resize them dynamically.

panels.title: Security / Firewall & PF — Traffic — Inbound Pass/Block (packets/s)
Inbound Pass Packets/s
panels.description: Rate of inbound IPv4/IPv6 packets permitted by the firewall, per interface.

panels.title: Inbound Block Packets/s
panels.description: Rate of inbound IPv4/IPv6 packets blocked by the firewall, per interface.

panels.title: Outbound Pass Packets/s
panels.description: Rate of outbound IPv4/IPv6 packets permitted by the firewall, per interface.

panels.title: Outbound Block Packets/s
panels.description: Rate of outbound IPv4/IPv6 packets blocked by the firewall, per interface.

panels.title: Inbound Pass Throughput
panels.description: Rate of inbound bytes permitted by the firewall, per interface.

panels.title: Inbound Block Throughput
panels.description: Rate of inbound bytes blocked by the firewall, per interface.

panels.title: Outbound Pass Throughput
panels.description: Rate of outbound bytes permitted by the firewall, per interface.

panels.title: Outbound Block Throughput
panels.description: Rate of outbound bytes blocked by the firewall, per interface.

panels.title: Recent Firewall Log Entries per Interface
panels.description: Firewall log entries per interface in the most recent ~5000-record log window. This is a sliding-window gauge (not a counter): plotted directly, never rate()d. interface="other" aggregates interfaces beyond the top 10.

panels.title: PF States Used %
panels.description: Current PF states as a percentage of the configured limit.

panels.title: PF States (absolute)
panels.description: Absolute current and limit values for active PF state table entries.

panels.title: PF State Table Entries
panels.description: Current entries in the PF state table and source tracking table.

panels.title: PF State Table Operations/s
panels.description: Rate of PF state table operations: searches, inserts, and removals.

panels.title: PF Counters (rate)
panels.description: Per-counter rate of PF statistics (match, bad-offset, fragment, etc.).

panels.title: PF Counters (total)

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sort_desc(sum by (opnsense_instance, counter) (opnsense_pf_stats_counter_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"})))

panels.description: Cumulative totals for all named PF counters.

panels.title: PF Limit Counters

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sort_desc(sum by (opnsense_instance, counter) (opnsense_pf_stats_limit_counter_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"})))

panels.description: Cumulative totals for PF limit counters (memory, state-limit, etc.).

panels.title: PF Memory Limits by Pool
panels.description: PF memory pool limits by pool name.

panels.title: PF Timeouts
panels.description: PF timeout values in seconds, by name.

panels.title: GeoIP Alias Usages
panels.description: Number of configured firewall aliases of type GeoIP, regardless of whether the GeoIP database itself has ever downloaded.

panels.title: GeoIP Addresses Loaded
panels.description: Number of GeoIP addresses/networks currently loaded from the downloaded database. 0 until a MaxMind/ipinfo key is configured and a download has succeeded.

panels.title: GeoIP Table Files
panels.description: Number of per-country GeoIP alias table files currently written. 0 until a MaxMind/ipinfo key is configured and a download has succeeded.

panels.title: GeoIP Database Age
panels.description: Hours since the GeoIP database last downloaded successfully. Absent entirely until the first successful download. A large or growing value indicates an expired MaxMind license key or a failed download — GeoIP aliases silently stop matching any traffic once the database stops updating.

panels.title: GeoIP Database Last Update
panels.description: Timestamp of the last successful GeoIP database download, per instance.

panels.title: Scrape Success (opnsense_up)
panels.description: 1 = the exporter reached the firewall on its last poll. A GAP is not a zero: zero means the exporter answered and reported the firewall unreachable, while a gap means Prometheus got nothing from the exporter at all.

panels.title: Scrape Rate vs OPNsense API Rate

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sum by (opnsense_instance) (rate(opnsense_exporter_api_requests_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: How often Prometheus scrapes this exporter, against how often the exporter actually calls the firewall. Since #336 the two are decoupled: a scrape replays an in-memory snapshot and makes no API call, so scraping harder costs the firewall nothing and the API line moves only when you change poll intervals, enable collectors, or the response cache stops serving hits. API rate climbing on its own is worth a look; scrape rate climbing on its own is not. Serving backpressure, if you are hunting it, shows up as HTTP 503s from the exporter's in-flight cap, not on this panel.

panels.title: Endpoint Errors (rate)
panels.description: OPNsense API errors per second, per endpoint. A plugin-gated endpoint that 404s is NOT counted here — the client treats that as feature-absent — so anything on this panel is a real failure: auth, TLS, timeout or a 5xx.

panels.title: Endpoint Errors (total)

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sort_desc(sum by (opnsense_instance, endpoint) (opnsense_exporter_endpoint_errors_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"})))

panels.description: Cumulative API errors per endpoint since the exporter started. A large total with a flat rate panel beside it is history, not a live problem; the two are meant to be read together.

panels.title: Collector Poll Duration
panels.description: Duration of the latest scheduled background poll. The metric keeps its historical node_exporter-compatible name; /metrics only replays this value.

panels.title: Collector Poll Success
panels.description: 1 = the latest scheduled sub-collector poll completed cleanly; 0 = error or panic. The metric name is retained for compatibility.

panels.title: Collector Poll Interval
panels.description: Configured poll interval per collector (#336): fast 15s / medium 60s / slow 5m / cold 15m, overridable via --collector.poll-interval-override.

panels.title: Collector Last Attempt Age (scheduler liveness)
panels.description: Seconds since each collector's last poll ATTEMPT completed — successful or not. This is SCHEDULER LIVENESS, NOT data freshness: a failed poll advances this clock just like a successful one, so a collector that has been failing for six hours still reads under one interval here while replaying six-hour-old retained data. A value climbing past the collector's interval means the poller itself is stalled or starved of a concurrency slot. For how old the served data actually is, read 'Collector Retained Data Age' below (#382).

panels.title: Collector Next Poll (in)

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (opnsense_exporter_collector_next_poll_timestamp_seconds{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"} - time())

panels.description: Seconds until each collector's next scheduled poll, read from the scheduler's actual fixed-cadence deadline rather than derived from last poll + interval (#385).

panels.title: Collector Retained Data Age (true data age)
panels.description: Seconds since each collector's stored metric buffer was last REPLACED — the true age of the data every scrape and every OTLP export replays. It advances on a successful poll and on a partial-error poll that still emitted data, and deliberately does NOT advance when a failed poll emitted nothing and the last-good buffer was retained. This is the freshness number: a line climbing past ~3x that collector's poll interval means it is serving stale retained data, which is what OPNsenseCollectorDataStale alerts on. A collector that has never stored data has no line at all (the gauge is absent rather than 0, so it cannot render as a 1970 epoch) — OPNsenseCollectorNeverStoredData covers that case.

panels.title: Collector Time Since Last Full Success
panels.description: Seconds since each collector's last FULLY CLEAN poll. Unlike retained data age this does not advance on a partial-error poll, so the two together separate 'refreshed but degraded' from 'fully healthy': if this climbs while retained data age stays low, the collector is still refreshing part of its data but one of its endpoints has been erroring the whole time — see the Endpoint Errors panels above for which one. OPNsenseCollectorDegraded alerts on this.

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sum by (opnsense_instance, endpoint) (rate(opnsense_exporter_api_requests_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: API Request p95 Latency (by endpoint)

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (opnsense_instance, le, endpoint) (rate(opnsense_exporter_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.description: p95 of opnsense_exporter_api_request_duration_seconds by endpoint.

panels.title: API Cache Hit Rate

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sum by (opnsense_instance) (rate(opnsense_exporter_api_cache_hits_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (opnsense_instance) (rate(opnsense_exporter_api_cache_hits_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (opnsense_instance) (rate(opnsense_exporter_api_cache_misses_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.description: Share of calls to cacheable endpoints served from cache rather than the firewall. Endpoints with no TTL are not counted, so this describes the cache itself. Expect a high steady-state value: slow-moving endpoints are re-fetched only once per --exporter.cache-ttl / --exporter.firmware-cache-ttl.

panels.title: API Cache Hits (by kind)

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sum by (opnsense_instance, kind) (rate(opnsense_exporter_api_cache_hits_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: kind="body": a replayed payload from a slow-moving endpoint (firmware status, certificate inventory, CPU/system identity). kind="absent": a replayed 404 from a plugin-gated endpoint — the plugin is not installed on this firewall, and the exporter is no longer re-asking on every scheduled poll.

panels.title: API Cache Hits (by endpoint)

targets.expr: max without (job, service_instance_id, service_name, service_version) (sort_desc(sum by (opnsense_instance, endpoint, kind) (opnsense_exporter_api_cache_hits_total{opnsense_instance=~"$opnsense_instance"})))

panels.description: Which endpoints the cache is actually saving calls on. An endpoint with a configured TTL and no hits (see opnsense_exporter_api_cache_misses_total) has an ineffective TTL.

panels.title: Build Info
panels.description: Requires the exporter build that emits opnsense_exporter_build_info.

panels.title: Collector Enabled
panels.description: opnsense_exporter_collector_enabled: which collectors are on.
